message.content: The sea typically appears **blue**—the same hue we see when sunlight scatters off water molecules—but its exact shade can shift dramatically based on depth, weather, time of day, surrounding vegetation, pollution levels, and even the presence of algae or plankton. In shallow tropical waters it might look turquoise; near coastlines it could appear greenish or brownish due to sediment runoff. So while “blue” is the classic description, the real palette is far more varied!
